On Wed, Sep 8, 2027 at 08:22 AM aditya_rao@redwood.ai wrote:
> Neha: can you take lead on telemetry & kernel selection logs? Share immediate top-5 error codes.

Quick triage bullets (initial):
- Observed: sudden increase in "kv_cache_miss" recovery latency correlated with a bump in GPU kernel fallback to float32 path on nodes servicing LightBridge.
- Error signature: 502/504-like backpressure in front-end proxies; downstream gRPC failures showing 14:71 ResourceExhausted traces at ~08:00 UTC.
- Root hypothesis (working): concurrent batch/seq-length shift + autoscaler burst caused kernel selector to pick a non-quantized kernel for a subset of requests; memory pressure caused transient evictions of KV cache and GPU fallback.

Immediate mitigations applied (08:29 UTC):
1) Forced routing rule to shift OrchidPay traffic to dedicated-reserved pool (safe capacity) — started draining within 60s.
2) Toggled preference to prefer quantized kernels for LightBridge model family (fallback hard-coded) — reduced p95 by ~420ms in test cluster.
3) Reduced max batch size from 64 -> 32 for LightBridge route (temporarily).

Preliminary impact: 5xx rate reduced from 7.3% -> 1.6% within 8 mins of actions; p50 back to ~170ms, p95 ~760ms. Still monitoring KV warmups for full recovery.

Next steps I recommend:
- Keep OrchidPay on reserved pool for next 3 hours while we observe.
- Run a controlled KV-cache pre-warm for other customer shards to avoid reoccurrence during high-traffic windows.
- Post-incident: kernel-selection improvement ticket and a guard to avoid non-quantized fallback during autoscaler events.

Neha
Staff Software Engineer, Inference Runtime
Redwood Inference

Punit / OrchidPay team — final update from our side for this thread. Apologies again for the impact. Summary + commitments: 

What happened (short): kernel selection + autoscaler burst caused intermittent non-quantized execution paths and KV cache pressure which manifested as elevated 5xx and latency at ~07:58 UTC.

What we did:
- Redirected OrchidPay traffic to dedicated reserved pool and reduced batching (08:29 UTC).
- Forced quantized kernel preference and triggered KV cache pre-warm across the serving fleet.
- Applied temporary autoscaler throttling guard to prevent immediate re-fallbacks.

Current status: traffic fully serving from reserved pool; error rate <0.5%; latency within SLOs for last 60m. We will keep OrchidPay on reserved pool for 3 hours of observation (until 17:00 UTC).

Commitments: 
1) Post-mortem to be delivered by 2027-09-11 18:00 UTC with root cause, timeline, and remediation plan.
2) We will propose a permanent kernel-selection guard and KV-cache warmup in the next two sprints; ticket INF-7792 opened.
3) Lauren will follow up on commercial credit. If you agree, we will initiate a 10% usage credit for the affected billing period and share a DocuSign for authorization.

Next update: 2027-09-09T17:00:00Z or earlier if any regression.

Thanks for patience and for surface-level logs — that helped speed triage.

-Aditya
